title: video.presence.spans_export
description: Cursor-paged snapshot of raw presence spans. Response: {"rows": [{"span_id", "room_key", "user_id", "connection_id", "joined_at", "left_at", "close_reason", "duration_seconds", "seq"}], "cursor": string|null, "total": integer|null} — the shape stapel_core.comm.projections._iter_snapshot pages through; `rows`, never `items`, because that reader looks for the key by name and an items-shaped answer rebuilds a consumer's table to EMPTY while reporting success. Paging is keyset over (joined_at, id), so a full walk visits every row exactly once even while the sweeper closes spans underneath it. `total` is reported on the first page only. `seq` is left_at (or joined_at, while open) in unix milliseconds — an Event's clock, so a live video.participant.left arriving mid-walk supersedes the snapshot row. left_at null means the connection is still open as far as this instance knows. Durations are RAW: no minimum is applied, since which stays count is the consumer's policy and baking it in would make a pricing change a code release.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from the previous page's `cursor`. Null/absent starts at the beginning.

limit.description: Rows per page. Absent/null means 500; values above 2000 are clamped.

period.description: Optional UTC calendar month filter, "YYYY-MM" — spans overlapping it. Absent exports everything retained.

period_start.description: ISO-8601 window start (inclusive), as an alternative to `period`.
